What degraded

  • The deck shipped under the bar at the round cap, median 7.124 against the 8.0 top rung.
    All three judges in all three rounds charged frames 2 to 5 as grey hardware and the benchmark told across two frames. Two recompositions moved the craft score less than 0.2, so the fault sits in the treatment chosen in the directors room.
  • No Texas place, public body or next step in the deck.
    The release carries no dateline and names Houston only in its site navigation, and cprit.texas.gov answered 403, so no claim supports a place or a CPRIT figure.
  • Merging frames 4 and 5 and a frame for a Texas stake were not made.
    Each needs a new composition, and the second needs a fetched source the run doesn't have.
  • tx-2026-0217 sits in Harris County on MD Anderson's home rather than a place the release names.
    The routine says never to guess a county from a decider's address, and Codex flagged it on PR 431. Holding the item would unbind the deck's record claims, so the county stays as tx-2026-0151 carries it and the item's note says what it rests on. A maintainer decides whether to hold it instead.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it SPACER, an AI model from MD Anderson, on what may keep T cells out of tumors, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Why do some tumors keep T cells out?

MD Anderson and other Texas institutions built an AI model called SPACER that helps explain where immune cells go and why they avoid some places. It reads gene activity across neighboring cells in intact tissue.

One answer may be mucins, sugar coated proteins many cancers make. They may help wall T cells off. In several melanoma and gastric cancer datasets more mucin was associated with poorer responses to checkpoint inhibitors. The release reports no diagnostic use.

SPACER ran on 37 datasets. In the team's benchmarking it was four to 21 times more effective than existing approaches at finding signals linked to cell recruitment. The Cancer Prevention and Research Institute of Texas helped fund the study.

Could a mucin reading tell a doctor whether a checkpoint drug will work?

#MDAnderson #CPRIT #SpatialTranscriptomics

Notes

The record. Re-verify stamped nine items: three by reverify.py with every claim unchanged (tx-2026-0118, tx-2026-0182, tx-2026-0212) and six checked by hand against the sources that answered (tx-2026-0062, tx-2026-0078, tx-2026-0079, tx-2026-0126, tx-2026-0138, tx-2026-0179). Twenty-four items sit behind a measured crawl boundary, re-measured October 15th with five days left on it, and are named unreachable rather than counted as rot. Admitted tx-2026-0217, MD Anderson's October 13th release on SPACER, eleven primary claims. Six leads are held for a later run, each needing its primary document: Plano's citywide AI initiative, the PUC's suit over its data center survey records, USDA's screwworm drone flights, Fermi America's AMD agreement at Project Matador, Mesquite and La Joya ISDs' AI drafting of special education plans, and UT Health San Antonio's dementia model study. The deck. Carousel no. 53 is nine material reliefs on one darkfield bench: a tumor nest walled by a glossy mucin coat with ember T cells halted outside, a 37 slide panorama across the swipe, the four to 21 benchmark at two scales, the uncoated nest where T cells press in, the mucin wall at macro, four cores by cancer type and mucin, and the slide back on a microscope stage with its funders engraved on the label. The audition was read seven times. The wall failed twice as a smooth extrusion and passed once it became a heap of glossy globules. The panel scored 6.986, 6.96 and 7.124, and the deck ships at the round cap under the 8.0 bar. Every judge charged frames 2 to 5 as grey hardware outside the tissue world and the missing Texas stake. None found a hard fail. Prompt audit, the reading that counts: 409 calls waited on the auto mode classifier, the longest 9.9 seconds, timed by the log itself and not a person. 1,914 tool calls measured, none waited on a human. No-stall hook: armed at 2026-10-17T05:08:23Z. At session start it judged the session unattended (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0), and the host's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED was 0. It refused nothing. The fetch side. keranews.org, mylubbock.us and hayscountytx.gov answered 403 during re-verify. www.cprit.texas.gov answered 403. nature.com served its abstract page to the scout and a client challenge to fetch_doc.py. All of it is in the sources field log. Review on PR 431. Codex found the record's summary calling all 37 datasets cancer datasets while c20 includes mouse heart, fixed. It found the payload and the topic ledger counts missing at an earlier head, both fixed before it posted. It found tx-2026-0217's Harris County resting on MD Anderson's address, which this routine forbids; the county stays, the item's note now says what it rests on, and the call is the owner's. It questioned tx-2026-0062's stamp with KERA unconfirmed; the routine allows a hand check on one primary source to set the stamp with the unconfirmed source named, which is what the note does.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
